key_insight: CareConnect shows that a tightly scoped, safety-first LLM agent can automate healthcare appointment logistics with high completion and strong guardrails.
clinical_relevance: It can reduce administrative burden and improve scheduling access while explicitly refusing medical advice, diagnosis, and emergency management.
method: Uses LLM function calling to execute eight domain-specific scheduling and information tools.
Adds retrieval-augmented generation for facility and workflow context.
Applies layered deterministic safety guardrails, including emergency detection and medical-intent refusal.
evidence_signal: In 680 task-oriented benchmark scenarios, the system achieved 91.8% task completion, 96.0% safety compliance on safety-critical cases, median latency of 2.2 seconds, and an average cost of $0.0324 per appointment.
watch_item: Performance depends on strict scope control, so real-world deployment would need careful monitoring for edge cases, emergency misuse, and integration with legacy scheduling systems.
paper_title: Toward Trustworthy Large Language Model Agents in Healthcare
